# SHSAT Prep for Parents: 2026 Adaptive Test Glossary


**TL;DR:** The SHSAT is NYC’s sole admissions test for eight specialized high schools, and it became a computer-adaptive test starting fall 2026. About 26,000 students compete for roughly 4,000 seats each year. This glossary breaks down every term parents encounter during SHSAT prep, from composite scores and cutoffs to the Discovery Program and Technology-Enhanced Items, all updated for the new digital format.


---


The SHSAT world is full of jargon. Composite scores, TEIs, forward-only navigation, the Hecht-Calandra Act. Prep companies assume you already know what these mean. You shouldn’t need to hire a tutor just to understand the vocabulary.


This glossary exists so you can orient yourself quickly and make better decisions about your child’s preparation. Whether you’re 18 months out or 10 weeks from test day, these are the terms that will come up in every conversation, every Reddit thread, and every prep book you open.


One important note before we start: the 2026 SHSAT is fundamentally different from every previous version. It moved from paper to computer-adaptive. If you took a standardized test yourself years ago, or if your older child prepped for a paper SHSAT, much of what you remember no longer applies.

## The Test Itself


### SHSAT (Specialized High Schools Admissions Test)


The SHSAT is the sole admissions test for eight of New York City’s most selective public high schools. There is no interview, no portfolio, no teacher recommendation, and no GPA requirement. Your child’s SHSAT composite score is the only factor that determines whether they receive an offer.


In the 2026 admissions cycle, 26,123 students took the SHSAT and 4,023 received an offer, an acceptance rate of just 15.4%.


Why this matters for you: everything in your child’s prep should be oriented toward maximizing this single score. Unlike college admissions, there are no other levers to pull.


### Specialized High Schools


Eight NYC public high schools admit students exclusively through the SHSAT. Here they are with their 2026 cutoff scores:


School Borough 2026 Cutoff


Stuyvesant High School Manhattan 561


High School of Math, Science & Engineering (HSMSE) Manhattan 539


Queens High School for the Sciences Queens 531


Bronx High School of Science Bronx 525


Staten Island Technical High School Staten Island 517


High School of American Studies (HSAS) Bronx 507


Brooklyn Technical High School Brooklyn 506


Brooklyn Latin School Brooklyn 495


For a deeper breakdown of what these numbers mean and how they shift year to year, see our[SHSAT cutoff scores guide](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/shsat-cutoff-scores-by-school) .


### Computer-Adaptive Test (CAT)


This is the single biggest change to the SHSAT in decades. On June 4, 2026, NYC Public Schools confirmed that the fall 2026 SHSAT will be a computer-adaptive test administered on DOE-provided computers.


What “computer-adaptive” means: the test adjusts its difficulty based on how your child answers. Get early questions right, and the test serves harder questions worth more toward the final score. Get early questions wrong, and the test offers easier ones, which limits the score ceiling.


This is why practitioners and tutors now emphasize accuracy over speed, especially in the first 8 to 12 questions of each section. The old strategy of skipping hard problems and coming back later? It no longer works for most of the test.


### Technology-Enhanced Items (TEI)


TEIs are question types that go beyond standard multiple choice. The 2026 SHSAT includes four families:


- **Drag-and-drop** : reorder steps in a math solution or arrange events from a reading passage
- **Multiple-select** : choose two or three correct answers (no partial credit is given)
- **Inline drop-downs** : select the correct word or expression from a dropdown menu embedded in a sentence or equation
- **Number-line and graph interactions** : click to place a point, drag a slider, or shade a region for an inequality


During the first digital SHSAT administration, many students reported that TEIs slowed them down. The content wasn’t harder. The unfamiliar format required adjustment. This means practicing with TEI-style questions is itself a prep task, separate from learning the actual math or ELA content.


### ELA Section


The English Language Arts section contains 50 questions and covers two areas:


**Revising and Editing** : You’ll see passages with errors or weak spots. Your child must identify and fix grammar, punctuation, sentence structure, and organization issues.


**Reading Comprehension** : Passages followed by questions testing understanding of main ideas, supporting details, vocabulary in context, author’s purpose, and logical inferences.


The ELA section tests skills that overlap with what your child will eventually need for the[digital SAT’s reading section](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/digital-sat-reading-and-writing-tips) , so strong SHSAT ELA prep builds a foundation for future tests too.


### Math Section


The Math section also contains 50 questions. Topics include:


- Ratios and proportional relationships
- The number system and expressions
- Equations and inequalities
- Statistics and probability
- Geometry


The math tested goes somewhat beyond typical 7th or 8th grade curriculum. Many questions require multi-step reasoning, not just formula recall. Students who have seen algebra concepts early have an advantage.


### Forward-Only Navigation


Here is something that catches many families off guard: on the 2026 adaptive SHSAT, students cannot go back and change answers on math questions or standalone ELA items once they advance to the next question.


The one exception is passage-based question sets in ELA. Within a single passage set, students can move back and forth. But once they submit the entire set, those answers are locked.


This rule makes the old “skip and return” strategy, which was a staple of paper SHSAT prep for years, largely obsolete. Parents on Reddit frequently discuss this change, with many noting that older prep books still teach the skip-and-return method. If your child’s prep materials don’t address forward-only navigation, they are outdated.


### Standard Testing Time


The SHSAT gives students 180 minutes (3 hours) total. There is no mandated break between sections.


Students can choose which section to start with, ELA or Math. This is a real strategic decision. Some tutors recommend starting with whichever section is your child’s stronger subject to build confidence and bank a high adaptive score early. Others suggest starting with the weaker section while mental energy is highest.


Three hours is a long time for a 13-year-old. Stamina, meaning the ability to maintain focus and accuracy for the full duration, is something that needs to be trained through timed practice sessions.


---


## Scoring and Admissions


### Raw Score


The raw score is simply the number of questions your child answers correctly in each section. On the 2026 test, the maximum raw score per section is 50.


### Scaled Score


The raw score is converted into a scaled score through a statistical process called equating. This accounts for slight differences in difficulty across test forms. Each section produces a scaled score ranging from 100 to 400.


You will never see your child’s raw score on the official report. Only scaled scores are reported.


### Composite Score


The composite score is the number that matters. It is calculated by adding the ELA scaled score and the Math scaled score together. The range is 200 to 800.


This composite score is what gets compared against cutoff scores to determine admission. For a detailed explanation of what score to aim for, read our[guide to good SHSAT scores](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/what-is-a-good-shsat-score-cutoffs-targets) .


### Cutoff Score


The cutoff score is the lowest composite score that earned an offer at a given school in a particular year. Cutoffs are not fixed. They shift annually based on the number of applicants, how they performed, and how many listed each school.


For the 2026 cycle, cutoffs ranged from 495 (Brooklyn Latin) to 561 (Stuyvesant). Your child needs to meet or exceed the cutoff for a school they ranked on their application to receive an offer.


### No Penalty for Wrong Answers


There has never been a penalty for wrong answers on the SHSAT, and the 2026 test is no exception. A blank answer and a wrong answer both score zero. There is never a reason to leave a question blank.


Tell your child this explicitly and repeatedly: guess on every question, even if it’s a complete shot in the dark. A random guess has a chance of being right. A blank has none.


### Score Predictor / Score Calculator


These are tools (offered by prep platforms and third-party sites) that estimate your child’s likely composite score based on practice test results. They help you gauge whether your child is on track for a particular school’s cutoff. A[score calculator](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/score-calculator) can also help you understand the raw-to-scaled conversion process, even though the exact formula varies by test administration.

## Prep Terms Parents Hear


### Diagnostic Test


A diagnostic test is a short assessment taken before any real studying begins. Its purpose is to identify your child’s specific strengths and weaknesses across ELA and Math topics.


This is the single most important first step in SHSAT prep for parents to arrange. Without a diagnostic, your child might spend weeks drilling topics they’ve already mastered while neglecting genuine weak spots. A[diagnostic test](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/diagnostic-test) creates the foundation for a targeted study plan rather than a generic one.


### Practice Test (Full-Length)


A full-length practice test simulates the actual SHSAT: same number of questions, same time limit, same digital format (ideally). Taking 8 to 10 timed practice tests before test day serves two purposes. First, it builds stamina and familiarity. Second, it reduces test anxiety. A student whose body has been through the 3-hour experience multiple times goes into test day with a dampened physiological alarm response because the situation is familiar.


For realistic timed practice in a digital format, check out[free SHSAT practice tests](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/best-free-shsat-practice-tests) to find options that match the 2026 format.


### Study Plan / Prep Timeline


Realistic SHSAT prep timelines look like this:


- **12 to 18 months** : students who start in spring of 7th grade (ideal)
- **6 to 9 months** : students who start the summer before 8th grade
- **About 10 weeks** : students who start after Labor Day of 8th grade (possible but very compressed)


Parents in r/SHSAT discussions consistently note that starting early allows for steady, low-pressure progress, while late starts force an intensity that can burn kids out. A[personalized study plan](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/study-plan-generator) helps structure the available time around your child’s specific needs.


### Prep Book vs. App vs. Tutor


These are the three main prep modalities, and the right choice depends on your child.


**Self-study with books and free DOE materials** is low-cost but requires strong student discipline and no major skill gaps. Community members on Reddit consistently report that self-study works well for kids who are already strong readers and internally motivated.


**App-based prep** offers adaptive practice, instant feedback, and structured study paths at a fraction of tutoring costs. This is where AI-powered platforms fit. For more on how AI-driven prep compares to free options, see our[Miyagi vs. Khan Academy comparison](https://miyagilabs.ai/compare/miyagi-vs-khan-academy) .


**Tutoring** helps most when a student has hit a plateau, has specific weak areas that self-study hasn’t resolved, or needs accountability. One-on-one tutoring is the most expensive option but provides the most personalized attention.


Many families combine modalities: an app for daily practice, a tutor for weekly check-ins on problem areas.


### Accuracy Over Speed


This is the single most important mindset shift for the 2026 adaptive test. Multiple practitioners emphasize that early questions carry outsized weight because they set the difficulty ladder. Getting the first 8 to 12 questions right in each section matters more than finishing quickly.


On the old paper SHSAT, speed mattered because all questions were worth the same and you could strategically skip. On the adaptive test, a student who rushes through early questions and gets several wrong may find themselves on a lower difficulty track, which caps their score potential regardless of how many later questions they answer correctly.


Prioritize accuracy during early-stage preparation. Speed comes naturally with mastery.


### NYC SHSAT Portal and Student Readiness Tool (SRT)


The NYC DOE provides an official practice platform with a Student Readiness Tool. The SRT is a tutorial that familiarizes students with the digital interface, including how to navigate questions, use the built-in tools, and interact with TEI formats.


Every student should go through the SRT before test day, regardless of how much other prep they’ve done. It’s free and takes about 30 minutes.

## Programs and Policies


### Registration Window


For the 2026-27 cycle, SHSAT registration runs from October 6 to October 30, 2026. Registration happens through your child’s school guidance counselor or online through the DOE system.


Missing the registration window means your child cannot take the test that year. Put it on your calendar now. For complete date details, see our[SHSAT test dates and deadlines](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/shsat-test-dates-registration-deadlines) page.


### School Day Administration


The SHSAT is primarily administered on a single “School Day” during the school day itself. For the current cycle, that date is November 18, 2026. Students take the test at their own school or a designated testing site on DOE-provided computers.


### MySchools


MySchools is the NYC DOE’s online platform where families manage high school applications and where SHSAT results and offers appear, typically in March. This is also where your child’s school ranking order is recorded during registration.


### Discovery Program


The Discovery Program gives economically disadvantaged students who score just below a school’s cutoff a second chance at admission. To be eligible, a student must meet all of the following criteria: come from a low-income household, be in temporary housing, or be an English Language Learner who arrived in NYC within the past four years; have scored within a defined range below the cutoff; and attend a high-poverty school.


Currently, the Discovery Program fills about 20% of seats at each specialized high school. Families do not apply separately. Eligibility is determined automatically based on the student’s SHSAT score and demographic information.


### DREAM Program (DREAM-SHSI)


DREAM-SHSI is a free DOE academic program that prepares eligible 7th graders to take the SHSAT in 8th grade. It provides tutoring, practice materials, and structured preparation at no cost.


This is one of the most underused resources available. If your child is in 7th grade and attends a school that participates, ask the guidance counselor about DREAM eligibility. Free, structured SHSAT prep for parents who might not otherwise be able to afford preparation is exactly what this program was designed for.


### Hecht-Calandra Act


The[Hecht-Calandra Act](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EDN/2590-H) of 1971 is the New York State law that codified the SHSAT as the sole admissions criterion for three of the specialized high schools: Stuyvesant, Bronx Science, and Brooklyn Tech. Because it is a state law, NYC cannot unilaterally remove the SHSAT. Any change would require action by the state legislature.


This is why, despite periodic political debates about the test, the SHSAT has remained in place for over 50 years and is likely to remain for the foreseeable future.


### Economic Need Index (ENI)


The Economic Need Index is a school-level poverty metric used by the DOE. It factors into Discovery Program eligibility. A student’s individual family income matters, but so does the poverty level of the school they attend. Schools with high ENI scores are more likely to have students who qualify for Discovery.


### Accommodations


Students with an IEP (Individualized Education Program) or 504 plan may receive testing accommodations such as extended time, additional breaks, or large print. These accommodations must already be documented in the student’s school records. You cannot request new accommodations specifically for the SHSAT. Since the test moved to digital format, accommodations are delivered digitally.


If your child has accommodations at school, confirm with the guidance counselor that they will transfer to SHSAT testing.


### LaGuardia High School


LaGuardia is technically the ninth specialized high school, but it does not use the SHSAT. Admission to LaGuardia is by audition in areas like music, drama, dance, art, and vocal performance. It is an entirely separate process. If you see “nine specialized high schools” mentioned somewhere, this is why the number is sometimes nine, sometimes eight.

## Common Parent Questions


### When should my child start SHSAT prep?


The ideal start is spring of 7th grade, giving you 12 to 18 months of steady, manageable preparation. Starting the summer before 8th grade (6 to 9 months out) is common and workable. Starting after Labor Day of 8th grade is possible but requires compressing a five-month plan into roughly ten weeks. For a structured approach, our guide on[how to study for the SHSAT](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-to-study-for-the-shsat) walks through timelines step by step.


### Are old paper prep books still useful for the 2026 test?


Partially. The underlying math concepts and reading skills haven’t changed, so the content review sections of older books remain useful. However, any strategy advice about skipping questions, returning to earlier items, or managing a 57-question-per-section format is now wrong. Prep books published before 2026 describe a test that no longer exists. Use them for content only, and supplement with digital, adaptive practice.


### Does my child’s school ranking order matter?


Yes. Students are only considered for the schools they list on their SHSAT registration form, and only in the order listed. If your child scores above the cutoff for their second-choice school but not their first, they’ll receive an offer to the second choice. If they don’t list a school at all, they cannot be offered a seat there, even if their score is high enough.


List every school your child would attend, in genuine order of preference. There is no strategic advantage to listing fewer schools.


### What if my child scores just below the cutoff?


If your child meets the eligibility criteria for the Discovery Program (low-income household, temporary housing, or recent ELL status, combined with attending a high-poverty school), they may still receive an offer. Discovery fills about 20% of seats and is applied automatically. You don’t need to apply separately.


If your child doesn’t qualify for Discovery and falls just short, the only option is to retake the SHSAT the following year if they are still in 8th grade or entering 9th grade, depending on the specific cycle rules.


### How should I manage test anxiety, both my child’s and my own?


It’s natural to want your child to succeed, but research on test anxiety makes one thing clear: kids are deeply tuned into their parents’ expectations. If they sense you have high hopes riding on test day, it compounds whatever anxiety they already feel.


The most effective anxiety reducer is repeated exposure. A student who has completed 8 to 10 full-length timed practice tests before the SHSAT goes in with a body and mind that have been through this experience many times. The physiological alarm response is dampened because the situation is familiar. Focus your energy on making sure your child gets plenty of realistic practice rather than talking about outcomes.


### Is the SHSAT the same as the SAT?


No. The SHSAT is a New York City test for high school admissions. The SAT is a national college admissions exam. They test different content at different levels. However, strong SHSAT preparation, especially in reading comprehension and algebra, does build a foundation that helps with the SAT years later.


### Can my child use a calculator on the SHSAT?


For the 2026 adaptive test, the DOE has not announced a calculator tool. Historically, calculators have not been permitted on the SHSAT. Students should prepare to do all math by hand or with whatever on-screen tools the DOE provides. Check the official DOE SHSAT page for the most current policy as test day approaches.


### What free resources are available?


The DOE’s Student Readiness Tool (SRT) is free and essential for familiarizing your child with the digital interface. The DREAM-SHSI program offers free structured prep for eligible 7th graders. Beyond that, community members on Reddit discuss free question banks and practice exams shared by various prep platforms. Our[free SHSAT practice test roundup](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/best-free-shsat-practice-tests) compiles the best options.
